text: “If only I had pretended to like the medicine,” was what Nana’s wet eyes said. “My liking for parties, George.” “My fatal gift of humour, dearest.” “My touchiness about trifles, dear master and mistress.” Then one or more of them would break down altogether; Nana at the thought, “It’s true, it’s true, they ought not to have had a dog for a nurse.” Many a time it was Mr. Darling who put the handkerchief to Nana’s eyes. “That fiend!” Mr. Darling would cry, and Nana’s bark was the echo of it, but Mrs.
